referenceBaseline.note: Latest official pages are used only for properties and contracts applicable to the frozen baseline; local experiments must record the exact runtime build.

sources.title: vSphere VMDirectPath I/O and Dynamic DirectPath I/O: Requirements for Platforms and Devices
claims: IOMMU and PCIe ACS are platform prerequisites for safe DMA remapping.
BAR, multifunction dependency, legacy bridge, P2P, RMRR, interrupt, PCI error, lifecycle, and device-count constraints are profile-dependent.
Suspend/resume, snapshots, Fault Tolerance, and vMotion are unavailable for VMDirectPath VMs.
Server, device, Guest OS, Guest driver, and workload support must be checked against compatibility and vendor guidance.
sources.limitations: Requirements and recommendations do not disclose the internal capability, placement, transaction, or recovery implementation.

sources.title: Configuring VMDirectPath I/O pass-through devices on an ESXi host
claims: Enabled and Active are distinct host states; an orange state may require reboot while green is enabled and active.
A VM with an assigned PCI device requires full configured-memory reservation.
Device-per-VM maximum depends on ESXi and virtual hardware version.
sources.limitations: UI and configuration guidance does not prove atomic owner transition or boot reconciliation internals.

sources.title: HostPciPassthruInfo
claims: The API exposes id, dependentDevice, passthruEnabled, passthruCapable, passthruActive, and optional hardwareLabel.
passthruCapable means vmkctl decided passthrough is possible; it is not a hardware compatibility-list support decision.
sources.limitations: No reason code or internal capable algorithm is exposed.

sources.title: HostPciDevice
claims: Host PCI inventory exposes BDF components, vendor/device/subsystem IDs, class, parent bridge, and device name with version-dependent additions.
sources.limitations: The API object is inventory, not an immutable snapshot or persistent physical-device fingerprint.

sources.title: VirtualPCIPassthroughDeviceBackingInfo
claims: Static backing identifies a physical PCI device with BDF id, vendorId, deviceId, and systemId.
sources.limitations: The public type does not prove how VMware detects same-BDF device replacement or stores a stronger fingerprint.

sources.title: HostAssignableHardwareManager
claims: The host API retrieves PCI devices usable for Dynamic DirectPath and updates assignable-hardware configuration.
sources.limitations: The API does not disclose global solver, reservation, lease, or fencing internals.

sources.title: VirtualMachineDynamicPassthroughInfo
claims: Dynamic candidate inventory exposes vendorId, deviceId, name, and optional customLabel.
sources.limitations: The object describes candidates, not selection order or atomicity.

sources.title: VirtualPCIPassthroughDynamicBackingInfo
claims: Dynamic backing contains allowedDevice selectors and optional customLabel.
assignedId is set to the selected physical device while powered on and is unset while powered off.
sources.limitations: No placement, fairness, retry, or multi-device transaction algorithm is exposed.

sources.title: VirtualPCIPassthroughAllowedDevice
claims: Dynamic selectors can match vendorId/deviceId and optionally subVendorId/subDeviceId/revisionId using values retrieved from a host or cluster.
sources.limitations: Selector syntax does not prove candidate ranking, resource-envelope, or dependency behavior.

sources.title: Broadcom Compatibility Guide - I/O Devices
claims: Production support is provided only for devices listed in the compatibility guide.
Listings represent devices physically tested or considered similar to tested devices.
sources.limitations: Listing status is a support contract and must not be treated as the runtime passthruCapable algorithm.

sources.title: HBA355i active storage paths prevent live PCI passthrough
claims: An active native storage consumer can make device detach Busy and prevent immediate owner transition.
Removing active paths, disabling the native driver, persisting configuration, and rebooting may be required for this exact profile.
sources.limitations: This device-specific consumer conflict must not be generalized into a universal reboot rule.

sources.title: VM power-on failure caused by insufficient PCI passthrough MMIO
claims: Insufficient PCI MMIO can fail VM power-on with a stable firmware error.
64-bit MMIO enablement and a power-of-two MMIO size are documented controls for large GPU BAR demand.
sources.limitations: The sizing example is operational guidance, not a complete general PCI topology allocator specification.

sources.title: DirectPath VM lifecycle-operation restrictions
claims: A VM with PCI DirectPath devices cannot live-vMotion, snapshot, suspend, or resume until the device is removed.
sources.limitations: The article does not describe internal lifecycle gating or Dynamic cold-relocation behavior.

sources.title: ESXi 8.0.3 strict ACS capability check workaround
claims: ESXi 8.0.3 can mark devices non-capable because of an overly strict ACS hierarchy sanity check.
disableACSCheck skips that strict check after reboot while ACS remains enabled.
sources.limitations: The workaround is not equivalent to Linux ACS override and does not prove a safe physical isolation domain.

sources.title: Dynamic DirectPath Content Library clone limitation and fix
claims: Some vCenter 7.0 U3 builds could not clone Dynamic DirectPath configurations to a Content Library template; the issue was fixed in a later patch.
sources.limitations: This version-specific defect is not a general Dynamic DirectPath architecture contract.

sources.title: ESXCLI hardware PCI passthrough command reference
claims: The supported host command surface exposes PCI passthrough inventory and configuration operations including immediate-apply behavior where available.
sources.limitations: Command syntax does not prove dependency atomicity, rollback, or boot reconciliation internals.

sources.title: HostPciPassthruConfig
claims: Host passthrough configuration identifies a PCI device, desired enabled state, and optional apply-now behavior.
sources.limitations: The configuration request does not expose the internal owner-transition transaction.

sources.title: HostCapability
claims: Host capability advertises platform support for passthrough and device rebind behavior.
sources.limitations: A host-level capability is not per-device qualification or HCL support.

sources.title: VirtualPCIControllerOption
claims: Virtual hardware configuration options expose runtime PCI passthrough device-count limits for the selected host and VM compatibility profile.
sources.limitations: The runtime query must be used for the exact ESXi/vHW pair; a documentation maximum must not be hard-coded as a universal limit.

sources.title: HostPciPassthruSystem
claims: The host managed object exposes passthrough state and configuration methods under explicit privileges.
sources.limitations: The public object is an operational surface, not a durable assignment journal or audit manifest.

sources.title: HostAssignableHardwareBinding
claims: Assignable Hardware exposes host-side bindings between dynamic device resources and VMs.
sources.limitations: The binding object does not disclose reservation linearizability, fencing tokens, or crash recovery.

sources.title: Best Practices for Performance Tuning of Latency-Sensitive Workloads in vSphere
claims: Dynamic DirectPath can participate in DRS initial placement and vSphere HA cold restart while live vMotion remains unavailable.
sources.limitations: The paper describes supported product behavior, not the placement, lease, consensus, or fencing implementation.

sources.title: VirtualMachineConfigInfo fixedPassthruHotPlugEnabled
claims: The API exposes fixedPassthruHotPlugEnabled from vSphere API 8.0.1, indicating a fixed passthrough hot-plug capability distinct from Dynamic power-on selection.
sources.limitations: Presence of the property does not establish supported device profiles, lifecycle safety, or the exact runtime behavior on the frozen lab baseline.

sources.title: ESXi hosts and compatible virtual machine hardware versions
claims: ESXi 8.0 U2/U3 can create, edit, and run virtual hardware version 21, while ESXi 8.0 and U1 cannot.
ESXi 8.0 U2/U3 can also create, edit, and run virtual hardware version 20.
sources.limitations: Compatibility with a virtual hardware version does not by itself establish the passthrough-device limit or Qman qualification for that ESXi/vHW pair.
